info.name: Dots on LiveKit Backend
info.description:
Postman collection for the **Dots on LiveKit** Python/FastAPI backend (`backend/`), built from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-30-dots-backend.md`.

## Setup
1. `cd backend && docker compose up -d postgres && uv run alembic upgrade head && uv run python scripts/seed.py`
2. `uv run uvicorn dots_backend.main:app --reload` (API on :8000)
3. Optional: `DISPATCH_MODE=fake uv run python -m dots_backend.worker` so tasks move QUEUED → RUNNING.
4. Import the `Dots Local` environment, then run **Agent API → Get user context by phone** first. It saves `userId` for every other request.

## Auth
- `/agent/*` (used by the `dot` and `dot-caller` agents): `Authorization: Bearer {{agentApiKey}}`
- `/api/*` (used by the UI): `X-User-Id: {{userId}}` (no real auth yet)

## Variables
| name | set by |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl`, `agentApiKey`, `demoPhone` | environment (`demoPhone` is the seeded demo user) |
| `userId` | *Get user context by phone* / *Get me* |
| `taskId` | *Create task (new Idempotency-Key)* |
| `idempotencyKey` | pre-request script on *Create task (new Idempotency-Key)* |
| `updatedSince` | *List tasks (all, updatedSince)* |

## Happy path
Run the **Agent API** folder top to bottom (or use the Collection Runner). It looks up the user, creates a task, replays the idempotency key, posts call events, posts a result, checks that a second result gets 409, then creates and cancels a second task.

`POST /api/session` returns 500 unless `LIVEKIT_API_KEY` / `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` are set in `backend/.env`. That is the only expected failure in a local run without LiveKit credentials.

## Out of scope for this backend version
No SSE (`/api/stream`), since the UI polls `GET /api/tasks?updatedSince=…`. No callback dispatch: `callbackStatus` stays `PENDING`, and there is no `/agent/tasks/:id/callback-status` endpoint yet.

item.name: Agent API (/agent)
item.description: Routes called by the `dot` voice agent and the `dot-caller` agent. Bearer auth.

request.description:
Dot's inbound-call lookup: resolve a caller's E.164 phone to their user context (user, memories, active tasks, 10 most recent finished tasks). A leading `+` in the path is fine.

**Saves `userId`** to the collection variables. 404 if no user has that phone.
Same payload as by-phone, keyed by user id. 404 if unknown.
Store a free-text memory for the user. Returns `201` with the `MemorySchema`. Memories show up (newest first) in the user context `memories` array.

Queue a `RESERVATION_CALL` task. **`Idempotency-Key` header is required** (422 without it); the pre-request script generates a fresh UUID into `idempotencyKey` each time you send this.

- `201` → new task created (status `QUEUED`)
- `200` → the key matched an existing task for this user; the existing task is returned

`payload.phone` must be E.164 and `payload.partySize` > 0 (422 otherwise). `callback` is stored but **not acted on** yet (`callbackStatus` stays `PENDING`).

**Saves `taskId`.**
Re-sends with the *same* `idempotencyKey` as the last "Create task (new Idempotency-Key)" call. Should return `200` and the same task id — no duplicate row.
Task plus its event timeline (oldest first). With the worker running, a freshly created task moves to `RUNNING` within ~2s once it's claimed and `dot-caller` is dispatched.

Called by `dot-caller` to append to the task timeline. Returns `204 No Content`.

`kind` is one of: `STATUS_CHANGED`, `CALL_DIALING`, `CALL_CONNECTED`, `TRANSCRIPT`, `NOTE`, `CALL_ENDED`, `CALLBACK_STARTED`, `CALLBACK_DELIVERED`, `ERROR`. `data` is optional free-form JSON.

Called once by `dot-caller` when the call is done. Finishes the task:

- `CONFIRMED`, `ALTERNATIVE_OFFERED` → `SUCCEEDED`
- `UNAVAILABLE`, `NO_ANSWER`, `VOICEMAIL`, `ERROR` → `FAILED`

**First result wins.** A second call (or a call on a canceled/finished task) returns `409`.
Simulates the caller agent's shutdown-hook safety net racing its normal path. Must be `409`.
The happy-path task above is already `SUCCEEDED`, so this makes a fresh one for the cancel request below. **Saves `taskId`.**
Cancel a `QUEUED` or `RUNNING` task → `CANCELED`. `409` if already final. In `DISPATCH_MODE=livekit` it also best-effort deletes the task's LiveKit room.

item.name: UI API (/api)
item.description: Routes called by the web UI. `X-User-Id` header.

request.description: Returns `{ "user": UserSchema }` for the `X-User-Id` header. No real auth yet — one seeded demo user.
Partial update — any of `name`, `phone`, `timezone`, `callbackDefaults`. Omitted fields are unchanged. Returns `{ "user": UserSchema }`.
The UI polls this instead of SSE. Newest first.

query.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only tasks with updatedAt strictly after this are returned

request.description:
Cheap polling: pass the max `updatedAt` you've already seen as `updatedSince` to get only changed tasks.

The test script stores the newest `updatedAt` from the response into `updatedSince`, so sending this repeatedly behaves like a real poller (empty list when nothing changed). Clear the `updatedSince` variable to start over.
Same shape as the agent-side `GET /agent/tasks/:id` — task + event timeline.
The UI can't create tasks (only Dot can), so this uses the agent route to make a fresh cancelable task. **Saves `taskId`.**
User-initiated cancel from the UI. `409` if the task is already final. (Unlike the agent route, this one does not delete the LiveKit room.)

Mints a LiveKit participant token for a new `session-<uuid>` room with the `dot` agent auto-dispatched via room config (metadata `{mode: "SESSION", userId}`).

Returns `{ serverUrl, participantToken, roomName }`. **Requires `LIVEKIT_URL` / `LIVEKIT_API_KEY` / `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET`** to be set on the server.

request.description: The header is required; missing it must not silently create an un-deduplicatable task.
FastAPI treats a missing required header as a validation error (422), not 401.
The contract the agent teammate generates a Python client from. Operation ids are the route function names (`create_task`, `get_task`, …).
Open in a browser for interactive docs.
